cases.prompt: During a wire-insulation overheating review, an engineer proposes using the usual ISS detector as proof every Teflon smoke case will raise an alarm. What did the flight experiment actually find?
A two-material suborbital test is cited to argue that the fabric which spread flames more slowly must also have gone out sooner. Did that particular comparison support the argument?
A reviewer enters 25% oxygen for a lunar-surface burn into a table of measured outcomes. Is there a finding to enter? Identify the sample and the status of this specific outcome.
A microgravity droplet video shows a large heptane flame disappear. Someone marks the timestamp as the end of combustion. Which additional observation changes that interpretation?
A designer equates a 5 cm wide Saffire fabric test with a 41 cm wide one because the fan speed was the same. Which observed spread rates can they cite, and what else differed?
Someone wants to enter one natural lunar airflow speed as a measured input for all upward fabric burns. What evidence can the lunar ignition study supply for that number?
